question.en: How do you apply Clean Architecture in a Flutter app?

keyPoints.en: Separate presentation, domain, and data responsibilities.
Keep domain rules independent of Flutter and data sources.
Use abstractions so outer layers can implement inner-layer needs.

answer.en: I separate the UI, business rules, and data access into clear layers. The domain layer contains the important rules and does not depend on Flutter widgets or a specific API. Repositories let the feature use data without tying its rules to one source.

followUp.en: How do you decide whether a feature needs a use case?

commonMistake.en: Do not add layers that only pass data through without improving separation or clarity.

question.en: What does the Single Responsibility Principle mean in practice?

keyPoints.en: A unit should have one focused reason to change.
Keep unrelated responsibilities in separate units.
Use cohesion and change impact to guide boundaries.

answer.en: I try to give a class or function one clear responsibility and one main reason to change. For example, a widget should not also parse API responses and decide business rules. I use this principle to make changes easier to understand and test, not to create a class for every line.

followUp.en: Can following this principle too strictly make a design worse?

commonMistake.en: Do not define the principle as a rule that every class can have only one method.

question.en: Which dependency direction helps keep domain rules independent?

options.en: Outer layers depend on abstractions owned by inner layers
Inner layers import concrete widgets from outer layers
Every layer imports every other layer directly
The domain depends on a specific remote API client

why.en: Inner business rules stay independent when outer details implement their abstractions.

tip.en: This makes it easier to replace data sources without changing domain rules.

quiz.source: Reason: This quiz checks how a focused responsibility limits unrelated reasons for a unit to change.

question.en: What is a useful sign that a class has too many responsibilities?

options.en: Unrelated changes often require editing the same class
The class has a descriptive name and one public method
The class is used by more than one feature
The class has a test for each public behavior

why.en: Unrelated reasons to change can indicate that responsibilities are coupled.

tip.en: Split responsibilities when doing so improves cohesion and change isolation.

question.en: What is a common role of a repository in an app architecture?

options.en: Provide data access behind a clear interface
Draw every feature screen and handle its gestures
Store all business rules inside a widget tree
Replace the need to model loading and failure

why.en: A repository separates data access details from the rest of the feature.

tip.en: A repository can coordinate local and remote data sources when needed.

question.en: When is a separate use case most valuable?

options.en: When a domain action needs a focused reusable boundary
Whenever a screen contains more than one widget
Whenever a model has a field that can be nullable
When an API response needs to be decoded as JSON

why.en: A use case can make meaningful domain actions explicit and independently testable.

tip.en: Avoid adding a use case that only forwards arguments without adding value.

question.en: A domain entity should import Flutter UI widgets to enforce a business rule.

why.en: Domain rules should not depend on presentation framework details.

tip.en: Keeping the domain framework-independent supports focused unit tests.
